subject: Availability attribution and latency exclusion — Shepherd private node pool
messages:
From: Michael Bryant <mbryant@shepherdtx.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+legal@shepherdtx.com, legal@shepherdtx.com
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Availability attribution for private node pool — Shepherd

Evelyn,

Thanks again for the call earlier. To summarize our ask on behalf of Shepherd Therapeutics: we're running Redwood Private in our on-prem cluster and will continue to own the top-of-rack networking, peering, and scheduled maintenance windows. Because network events on our side can cause elevated tail latency and occasional node disconnections, we need an appendix to the SLA that attributes availability/latency exceptions to Shepherd-managed network incidents and excludes them from Redwood uptime calculations when evidence is provided.

I've attached a diagram of our topology (network-drawings.pdf) and a draft appendix Shepherd's legal team started (proposed-sla-appendix-v1.docx). High level asks:
- Exclusion of network-induced latency/outages originating from customer-owned routers/peering links.
- A documented evidence checklist Redwood can use to validate claims.
- A clause for timely telemetry-sharing (SNMP/Netflow or logs) to enable root cause attribution.

We're ready to share a sample incident report template. Can Redwood confirm the types of telemetry that will satisfy the evidence checklist (bandwidth graphs, interface error counters, flow logs, timestamps aligned to Redwood request traces)? Also please advise on any alternative mitigations Redwood recommends to avoid a hard exclusion (e.g., passive monitoring, synthetic probes).

Michael
Michael Bryant
VP Ops, Shepherd Therapeutics
mbryant@shepherdtx.com
+1 415-555-0198

Attachments: network-drawings.pdf (PDF), proposed-sla-appendix-v1.docx (DOCX)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Michael Bryant <mbryant@shepherdtx.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, legal@shepherdtx.com
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Availability attribution for private node pool — Shepherd

Michael — thanks for the clear write-up and the attachments. Appreciate the topology diagram.

Quick acknowledgement of next steps from our side:
1) Technical review: Marcus will map the topology to our request trace correlation and propose an evidence checklist.
2) Legal / contract: I'll work with contracts to draft an SLA appendix that defines the exclusion criteria and the required artifacts.
3) Operationally: Aditya will assess what telemetry integrations we can accept (NetFlow, sFlow, SNMP counters, packet captures with redaction).

Prelim notes: Redwood's goal is to preserve customer availability guarantees where we control the stack and attribute exceptions where the customer controls the causal component. We are open to an "availability attribution" approach rather than a blanket exclusion — i.e., when Shepherd provides verifiable evidence that the root cause is customer-managed networking, Redwood will mark the window as excluded for uptime calculations; during inconclusive windows we propose a joint investigation window (72 hours) before exclusion.

Can you confirm Shepherd's SLA contact for the telemetry handoff (SRE or netops) and whether you can deliver interface-level counters at 1-minute granularity for the incident windows? It will help us specify exact telemetry fields in the appendix.

I'll circulate a proposed appendix draft by COB Monday for your review.

Evelyn Hart
Director, Enterprise Success — Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.com

Subject: RE: Availability attribution for private node pool — Shepherd (technical notes)

Evelyn/Aditya — following up with a technical handoff and proposed checklist we can include in the appendix. Draft below; feel free to edit.

--- Proposed attribution checklist (technical) ---
1) Temporal alignment: customer network event timestamp window (start/end) with per-minute granularity mapped to Redwood request traces (trace ids + timestamps).
2) Interface counters: if index-of-failure is a router/switch, provide: interface input/output errors, drops, resets, and BGP flap history for the involved interfaces for +-30 minutes.
3) Flow evidence: NetFlow/sFlow summary showing traffic blackholing or misannounced prefixes.
4) Passive probe/synthetic: If available, provide synthetic probe logs (ICMP/TCP latency) from at least 2 vantage points internal to Shepherd to show host reachability loss.
5) Corroboration: Customer incident report signed by Shepherd netops with description of the control-plane change (if any), maintenance schedule, and relevant ticket ids.

Exclusion decision rules (suggested):
- If checklist items 1,2 and 5 are provided and show clear network-side degradation, mark the window "customer-attributed" and exclude from Redwood uptime SLA.
- If evidence is partial, open joint investigation (48-72h). If investigation inconclusive within 72h, record as disputed and escalate to ops leadership for triage.

Operational considerations:
- We'll need a secure upload path (S3 pre-signed link or secure Drive) and a redaction policy for PCAPs.
- For latency exclusions (not outage), we should define measurable thresholds (p99 increase > 200ms over baseline) and a minimum sustained duration (5 minutes) to avoid noise.

If these look reasonable I can turn them into tight contract language for legal to paste into the appendix.

- Marcus
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Availability attribution for private node pool — Shepherd

Michael — thanks, and appreciated Marcus's quick turnaround. We can proceed with the approach below and I'll capture it in the appendix draft for legal. Action items and timeline:

- Shepherd to confirm telemetry contact and provide interface counters/NetFlow snapshots for any incident windows (deliverable: Shepherd netops contact + test sample by Wed 2027-10-20).
- Redwood to publish exact telemetry fields we accept and a secure evidence upload flow (deliverable: proposed appendix draft sent to Shepherd legal by Mon 2027-10-18).
- Agreement on exclusion decision rules as drafted by Marcus; disputed windows escalate to ops leadership within 72h.

Proposed compromise to speed mutual acceptance: Redwood will accept an operational mitigation alternative in lieu of a formal exclusion if Shepherd implements one of the following for the node pool: (A) an active synthetic probe fleet managed by Shepherd with logs forwarded to Redwood in near real-time, or (B) a lightweight BGP/peering health telemetry stream (1-min samples) that Redwood ingests. If Shepherd takes either option and provides retention for 90 days, Redwood will not require a permanent exclusion clause and instead treat incidents under the shared monitoring model as "jointly managed" for SLA calculations.

I'll attach the appendix draft to the DocuSign packet and include the evidence checklist. Please confirm Shepherd's preferred path (formal exclusion + checklist vs. joint-monitoring alternative).

Thanks — looking forward to closing this for the SHEP-4381 deployment.

Evelyn Hart
